NO

YES TO ALL 
NO 
NO TO ANY

CANADIAN C-SPINE RULE 
ANY HIGH-RISK FACTORS? 
• Age > 65 
• Focal peripheral neurological deficit or paraesthesias 
• Dangerous mechanism of injury: 
o Pedestrian or cyclist struck by vehicle 
o MVA with Ejection from vehicle/High speed/Roll-over 
o Fall from height > 1m or 5 stairs 
o Axial load to head e.g. diving 
o Quad-bike accident 
 
Is there any indication to do a CT-Brain 
as per Head Injury protocol? 
 
If YES: 
Perform non-contrast CT-Brain AND 
C-spine 
 
 
AT LEAST ONE LOW RISK FACTOR? 
 
• Involved in simple rear-end MVA 
• Is comfortable in sitting position in ED 
• Has been ambulatory at any time since injury 
• Presented with delayed onset of neck pain 
• ABSENCE OF MIDLINE NECK TENDERNESS 
 
YES 
 
 Able to rotate neck 45 left and right? 
 
NOT APPLICABLE IF: 
• Non-trauma pain 
• GCS < 15 
• Unstable vitals 
• Age < 16 
• Acute paralysis 
• Known vertebral disease 
• Previous C-spine surgery 
• Pregnant 
NEXUS CRITERIA 
 
• GCS 15 and stable 
• No focal neuro deficit 
• No altered LOC 
• No intoxication 
• No midline spinal tenderness 
• No distracting injury 
 
If all of the above criteria are met, 
NO indication for C-spine imaging 
 
NB LESS RELIABLE IF AGE > 65  
 
RADIOGRAPHY – CT C-SPINE 
NO ROLE FOR X-RAYS IF CT 
AVAILABLE 
 
 NO IMAGING REQUIRED
